facts.text: The seeds of nationalism were sown by the reforms of the newly educated society, creating a favourable situation for an all India political organisation.
facts.quote: The seeds of nationalism were sown by the reforms of newly educated society. Due to various movements in different parts of India a favourable situation was created to build a political organisation on an all India level

facts.text: Centralisation of administration: identical reforms and equality before law developed nationalism; roads and railways built by the British also benefited Indians.
facts.quote: Due to identical reforms all over the country and equality before law, the feeling of nationalism developed among the people. For the convenience of administration and swift movement of the army the British built network of roads and railways. But these facilities benifited the Indians as well.

facts.text: Economic exploitation: Indian wealth flowed to England; farmers were compelled to take cash crops and traditional industries declined.
facts.quote: The Indian wealth was flowing towards England by all means. ... Farmers were compelled to take cash crops, burden of land taxes, continuous famines ... Traditional industries declined which led to rise in unemployment.

facts.text: Western education introduced ideas such as Justice, Liberty, Equality, Democracy; English gave India a new medium of communication.
facts.quote: Due to spread of western education, new ideas such as Justice, Liberty, Equality, Democracy etc. were introduced to the Indians. ... with the introduction of English language India got a new medium of communication.

facts.text: The 'Asiatic Society' was established at Kolkata by the British; manuscripts in Sanskrit, Persian and other languages were examined.
facts.quote: The 'Asiatic Society' was established at Kolkata by the British. ... The manuscripts in Sanskrit, Persian and other languages were examined and research was published.

facts.text: Dr.Bhau Daji Lad and Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar made an intensive study of ancient Indian culture; Indians were awakened with a sense of Identity.
facts.quote: Indian scholars like Dr.Bhau Daji Lad, Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar made intensive study of ancient Indian culture. After understanding that we are blessed with glorious ancient tradition, the Indians were awakened with a sense of Identity.

facts.text: The 'Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute' has been working for the last 100 years in Pune.
facts.quote: The 'Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute' is working since last 100 years in Pune.

facts.text: Newspapers like Darpan, Prabhakar, Hindu, Amrit Bazar Patrika, Kesari and Mahratta started criticising the Government.
facts.quote: Newspapers like Darpan, Prabhakar, Hindu, Amrit Bazar Patrika, Kesari, Mahratta started criticising the Government.

facts.text: On 28 December 1885, the first session of Indian National Congress was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School in Mumbai.
facts.quote: On 28 December 1885, the first session of Indian National Congress was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School in Mumbai.

facts.text: 72 delegates from different provinces of India participated in the first session.
facts.quote: 72 delegates from different provinces of India participated in this session.

facts.text: Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee, a renowned lawyer from Kolkata, was the President of the first session.
facts.quote: Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee, a renowned lawyer from Kolkata, was the President of this session.

facts.text: Allan Octavian Hume, a British officer, took lead in the establishment of the Indian National Congress.
facts.quote: Allan Octavian Hume, a British officer, took lead in the establishment of the Indian National Congress.

facts.text: Objectives of the Congress: make people forget differences, bring them on a common platform, increase the feeling of oneness and work for development.
facts.quote: To make the people from different parts of India forget the differences in religion, race, caste, language, geographical territories and bring them on a common platform, ... to increase the feeling of oneness among the people, to take efforts for the development of the country

facts.text: Moderate Phase (1885-1905): the leaders were realistic and highly educated and believed in constitutional methods.
facts.quote: Moderate Phase (1885-1905) : ... The leaders of Indian National Congress were realistic and highly educated. ... They believed in constitutional methods.

facts.text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Ferozshah Mehta and Surendranath Banerjee were moderate leaders.
facts.quote: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Ferozshah Mehta, Surendranath Banerjee were all moderate leaders.

facts.text: Moderate resolutions included representation in provincial legislature, jobs for educated Indians, cutting military expenses and separating Legislature and Judiciary.
facts.quote: to get representation in provincial legislature, jobs for educated Indians, cutting down the increasing expenses on military, Legislature and Judiciary should be seperated for safeguarding legal rights of Indians etc.

facts.text: Extremist Phase (1905-1920): Extremists believed in severe struggle; Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal were extremist leaders.
facts.quote: The Moderates who advocated peaceful and constitutional manners and the Extremist who believed in severe struggle for attainment of freedom. Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal were believed to be extremist leaders.

facts.text: Early on, Extremist leaders used newspapers, national festivals and national education for political awakening.
facts.quote: the Extremist leaders, for bringing political awakening among the Indians used methods like newspapers, national festivals and national education.

facts.text: 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' were the newspapers through which Lokmanya Tilak criticised the British; 'Amrit Bazar Patrika' was the mouthpiece of extremist ideology in Bengal.
facts.quote: 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' were the newspapers through which Lokmanya Tilak made severe criticism on the suppressive policy of the British. In Bengal province, 'Amrit Bazar Patrika' was a mouthpiece of extremist ideology.

facts.text: Tilak started organising Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav; he felt the government would not ban people coming together for religious reasons.
facts.quote: with these objectives Tilak started organising of Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav. For political reasons if people come together then government will ban them, but for religious reasons if people come together the government will not ban them was his opinion.

facts.text: In the Mandalay prison, Tilak wrote 'Geeta-rahasya', whose core was the philosophy of karmayoga.
facts.quote: In the Mandalay prison, Tilak wrote 'Geeta-rahasya'. Its core was philosophy of karmayoga

facts.text: The extremists did not adopt armed revolution but insisted on extensive public agitation; the moderates laid the foundation and the extremists carried the movement forward.
facts.quote: But they did not adopt the means of armed revolution rather insisted for an extensive public agitation. The moderates laid the foundation of freedom movement and the extremists carried forward the movement.

facts.text: In 1897 plague spread in Pune; officer Rand adopted oppressive measures and the Chapekar brothers assassinated him; the government imprisoned Tilak.
facts.quote: In 1897, in Pune, the epidemic of Plague had spread on a large scale. ... An officer named Rand was appointed. ... As a revenge, the Chapekar brothers assasinated Rand. ... the government imprisoned Tilak with revenge.

facts.text: In 1905, Viceroy Lord Curzon declared the partition of Bengal province, with majority Muslims in East Bengal and majority Hindus in West Bengal.
facts.quote: The then Viceroy Lord Curzon contributed to it. ... in 1905, he declared the partition of Bengal province. With this partition, arrangement was made such that majority Muslims will remain in East Bengal and West Bengal for majority of Hindus.

facts.text: 16 October, the day of partition, was observed as National Mourning Day; 'Vande Mataram' was sung and 'Raksha Bandhan' programmes were held as a symbol of unity.
facts.quote: 16 October, the day of partition was observed as National Mourning Day. ... 'Vande Mataram' came to be sung everywhere. As a symbol of unity, 'Raksha Bandhan' programmes were held.

facts.text: The anti partition movement was led by Surendranath Banerjee, Anand Mohan Bose, Rabindranath Tagore and others; the British annulled the partition.
facts.quote: The leadership of this movement was in the hands of Surendranath Banerjee, Anand Mohan Bose, Rabindranath Tagore and such other leaders. ... the British anulled the partition of Bengal.

facts.text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the President of the Indian National Congress session of 1905 and supported the anti partition movement.
facts.quote: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the President of Indian National Congress session of 1905. He supported the anti partition movement.

facts.text: Dadabhai Nowrojee was the President of the 1906 session and for the first time pronounced the word 'Swaraj' from the stage.
facts.quote: Dadabhai Nowrojee was the President of 1906 session. For first time he pronounced the word 'Swaraj' from the stage.

facts.text: In the same (1906) session, the 4 point programme of Swaraj, Swadeshi, National Education and Boycott was unanimously accepted.
facts.quote: In the same session Swaraj, Swadeshi, National Education and Boycott, this 4 point programme was unanimously accepted by the Indian National Congress.

facts.text: Boycotting foreign goods was the first step and boycott of foreign rule the next step.
facts.quote: It was decided that boycotting of foreign goods is the first step and boycott of foreign rule will be the next step.

facts.text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905.
facts.quote: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905.

facts.text: The differences between Moderates and Extremists rose greatly in the Surat session in 1907, ending in a split in the Indian National Congress.
facts.quote: The differences between the ideologies of Indian National Congress rose to great extent in the Surat session in 1907. ... finally there was a split in the Indian National Congress.

facts.text: At Surat, Lala Lajpat Rai tried to act as a mediator; Tilak felt the Congress was a national platform and should not be divided.
facts.quote: Lala Lajpat Rai tried to act as a mediator. As per Tilak's opinion, Indian National Congress was a national platform, hence it should not be divided.

facts.text: Suppression: public meetings were banned, restrictions were put on newspapers and many printing presses were confiscated.
facts.quote: Holding of public meetings was legally banned. ... Many restrictions were imposed on newspapers. Many printing press were confiscated

facts.text: Tilak advocated the bomb attacks through Kesari; charged with sedition, he was sent to Mandalay jail at Myanmar for 6 years imprisonment.
facts.quote: These bomb attacks were advocated through Kesari newspaper by Lokmanya Tilak. The charge of sedition was put on Lokmanya Tilak for which he was sent to Mandalay jail at Myanmar for 6 years imprisonment.

facts.text: Bipin Chandra Pal was sentenced to jail and Lala Lajpat Rai was deported from Punjab.
facts.quote: Bipin Chandra Pal was sentenced to jail and Lala Lajpat Rai was deported from Punjab.

facts.text: A committee of upper class Muslims under Aga Khan met Governor General Lord Minto; the Muslim League was established in 1906.
facts.quote: a committee of upper class Muslims under the leadership of Aga Khan met Governor General Lord Minto. Due to the motivation from Lord Minto and other British officers, the Muslim League was established in 1906.

facts.text: The Morley Minto Reform Act of 1909 increased Indian members in the Legislative Assembly and gave separate electorates to Indian Muslims.
facts.quote: the Morley Minto Reform Act of 1909 was passed. According to this act, it increased the number of Indian members in the Legislative Assembly ... In the same act seperate electorates were provided to the Indian Muslims.

facts.text: The Lucknow session of the Congress was held in 1916; in the same year the Congress and the Muslim League made an agreement known as the 'Lucknow Pact': the Congress agreed to separate electorates for Muslims and the League agreed to support the Congress.
facts.quote: In the Lucknow session of Indian National Congress in 1916, under the leadership of Lokmanya Tilak, an attempt was made to resolve the dispute in the Indian National Congress. In the same year there was an agreement between Indian National Congress and Muslim League known as the 'Lucknow Pact'. According to this pact, the Indian National Congress agreed to seperate electorates to Muslims and Muslim League agreed to support the Indian National Congress

facts.text: In 1914, when Lokmanya Tilak was released from the Mandalay Jail, the first world war had begun in Europe.
facts.quote: In 1914, when Lokmanya Tilak was released from the Mandalay Jail, the first world war had begun in Europe.

facts.text: Dr. Annie Besant and Lokmanya Tilak started the Home Rule movement; Home Rule means self government; a similar movement began in Ireland.
facts.quote: Dr. Annie Besant and Lokmanya Tilak started the Home Rule movement. Home Rule means self government. Such movement also began in Ireland against Colonialism.

facts.text: Tilak firmly stated, 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.
facts.quote: Tilak firmly stated that, 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.

facts.text: In 1917, Montague, Secretary of State for India, declared that Indians would be given self government step by step.
facts.quote: In 1917, Montague, Secretary of State for India, declared that step by step Indians will be given the right to self government and responsible political system.

facts.text: Tilak's policy of co-operating only if the government showed sympathy to Indian demands is known as 'Responsive Cooperation'.
facts.quote: Tilak also declared that if the government is going to show sympathy and considerable attitude towards the demands of the Indians, only then Indian public is ready to co-operate the British. This policy of Lokmanya Tilak is known as 'Responsive Cooperation'.

facts.text: In 1919, the British Parliament passed the 'Montague Chelmsford Reform Act'; Finance, Home affairs and Revenue stayed under the Governor.
facts.quote: In 1919, the British Parliament passed another act ... This act is known as 'Montague Chelmsford Reform Act'. ... the important departments like Finance, Home affairs and Revenue were under the control of the Governor.

facts.text: Tilak criticised the 1919 Act: 'This is neither Swaraj nor its foundation'.
facts.quote: Tilak criticised the act in following words, 'This is neither Swaraj nor its foundation'.
